page.overview:
Who is Heimlich?

Heimlich is a character in A Bug's Life.

Heimlich is an obese lime caterpillar with a German accent who works as a clown in P.T. Flea's circus troupe. He is very gluttonous and always seems to be eating. Even during a performance, he offered to help finish one of the audience's candy corns. The fly refused, but then it turned out that he got the candy corn anyway. He then later calls the flies out as Francis argues with them.

At the beginning of the film, Heimlich says that he dreams of being a beautiful butterfly. At an unspecified point following the film's climax, he finally pupates, ultimately emerging from his cocoon during the film's final scene. On emerging, however, Heimlich's appearance and morphology as a butterfly are shown to almost exactly mirror those of his caterpillar form, the only differences being his newfound blue body coloration, the loss of the orange ornamentation on his back and the presence of a miniscule pair of wings. Owing to both his wings' small size and his continued obesity, Heimlich therefore remains flightless even in his adult form, and it takes the efforts of Francis, Manny, Flik, and a few other ants to get him up in the air. Whilst a caterpillar, Heimlich was carried by the rhino beetle, Dim, for transport.

Heimlich is shown to have a gluttonous appetite and is seen eating almost all the time, especially while helping the ants construct a bird to scare Hopper and his gang. Although brave, he still shows fear when a real bird nearly eats him. Also, when Hopper shouts at the approaching circus wagon, he frightens Heimlich who says he thinks he's going to wet himself.
